messages.subject: [Picante-devel] evolve.trait() hidden?
messages.body_plain:
Hey all,

I haven't been keeping up with the blow by blow of picante, so
apologizes if this has already been discussed.   I was planning on
adding some code David wrote to the evolve.trait() function.  I notice
that it is currently a hidden function, what is the plan for the
function?  Does it need some work before we want to expose it more?
Slated for removal?  Other?

cheers

Peter

messages.subject: [Picante-devel] evolve.trait() hidden?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,

I hid evolve.trait because I didn't get around to writing proper  
documentation for it. Feel free to modify, un-hide, work on the docs,  
etc..

We should also do a bit of testing with geiger's fit.continuous to see  
if the different modes of trait evolution in evolve.trait generate the  
expected patterns.

Cheers,
Steve

messages.subject: [Picante-devel] picante 0.3 on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
(Whoops, sent this email to the phylobase listserv by accident!)

Just uploaded picante 0.3-0 to CRAN. This release has some bugfixes to
PSV/etc. and evolve.trait, and adds Matt's new functions for
phylogenetic community-environment regressions and phylogenetic
bipartite linear models.

The pbglm function has an option to use code from the brglm library,
this library is included as a 'suggested' package with code in the
function to check and warn if the library is not loaded.

Nice work all!

I will soon update the tracker on R-Forge soon with the "to do" items
from the TODO file from the svn repos and delete that file. Let's move
discussion and tracking of new features to the tracker. If you haven't
already, you may want to log in to R-Forge and monitor the trackers
and discussion forums.

Steve
